label: Platonism
description: Eternal Forms, the Good, reason ascending past appearances.
plain: Ideas from the Greek philosopher Plato. He taught that the things we see are imperfect copies of perfect, unchanging patterns he called Forms.

label: Aristotelianism
description: Natural ends, categories, virtue as habit, logic from observation.
plain: Ideas from Aristotle, Plato's student. He studied the natural world closely and argued that everything has a purpose it grows toward.

label: Stoicism
description: Rational cosmic order, virtue as the only good, mastery of passions.
plain: An ancient Greek and Roman school. Stoics taught that the universe runs on reason and that a good life means staying calm and doing your duty.

label: Christianity
description: Incarnation, grace, sin and redemption, the Church.
plain: The religion built on the life and teaching of Jesus. Its core ideas include sin, forgiveness through God's grace, and salvation.

label: Gnosticism
description: Flawed material world, hidden saving knowledge, divine spark trapped in matter.
plain: Early religious groups who taught that the physical world is a trap made by a lesser god, and that secret knowledge (gnosis) sets the soul free.

label: Hermeticism
description: As above, so below; correspondences, occult knowledge, the magus.
plain: A tradition based on texts credited to a legendary sage, Hermes Trismegistus. Its motto is 'as above, so below': the heavens and earth mirror each other.

label: Enlightenment liberalism
description: Individual rights, consent, reason, progress, limited government.
plain: The 1600s–1700s movement that championed individual rights, free thought, government by consent of the people, and progress through reason.

label: Marxism
description: Material conditions, class struggle, history as dialectical motion.
plain: Ideas from Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. They argued that conflict between economic classes drives history and that capitalism will give way to communism.

label: Darwinism
description: Variation, selection, descent with modification, no designer needed.
plain: Charles Darwin's theory that living things change over generations: those best suited to their surroundings survive and pass on their traits.

label: Nietzsche
description: Will to power, revaluation of values, death of God, the overman.
plain: Ideas from the German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche. He attacked Christian morality, declared 'God is dead', and urged people to create their own values.

label: Critical theory
description: Exposing power hidden in norms, institutions and culture.
plain: A school of thought that grew out of the Frankfurt School in Germany. It looks for hidden power in everyday rules, institutions and culture, and asks who benefits.

label: Confucianism
description: Ritual, filial duty, humane rule, cultivated character.
plain: Ideas from the Chinese teacher Confucius. He taught that a good society rests on family duty, proper ritual and rulers who lead by moral example.

label: Daoism
description: The Way (Dao), effortless action, simplicity, harmony with nature.
plain: A Chinese tradition built on the Tao Te Ching. It teaches following the Dao, the natural Way of things, by acting simply and without force.

label: Buddhism
description: Suffering, impermanence, no fixed self, liberation through the Middle Way.
plain: The tradition begun by the Buddha in India. It teaches that suffering comes from craving and that a disciplined path of ethics and meditation ends it.

label: Vedanta
description: Brahman (ultimate reality), Atman (the self), liberation through knowledge.
plain: Indian philosophy built on the Upanishads. Its central idea is that the deepest self (Atman) is linked to, or the same as, ultimate reality (Brahman).

label: Islamic philosophy
description: Greek philosophy recast in Arabic: reason, God, emanation, the intellect.
plain: Philosophy in the medieval Islamic world. Thinkers like al-Kindi and Avicenna took up Aristotle and Plato and joined them with belief in one God.

label: Islam
description: Revelation to Muhammad, the Quran, tawhid, law and the mystical path.
plain: The religion founded on the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad in 7th-century Arabia.

label: Judaism
description: Covenant, Torah, the Hebrew Bible and rabbinic law.
plain: The religion and tradition of the Jewish people, built on the covenant with God and the Torah.

label: Romanticism
description: Feeling, imagination, nature, the folk and the inner self over cold reason.
plain: The movement of the late 1700s and 1800s that prized feeling, imagination, nature and folk culture.

label: Nationalism
description: The nation as the main unit of loyalty and the rightful basis of the state.
plain: The belief that each nation should rule itself and that loyalty to the nation comes first.

label: Humor
description: Joke, play and laughter as the medium of the idea.
plain: Not a school of thought but a style: how much the idea lives in jokes, play and laughter.

label: Irony
description: Saying one thing and meaning another; distance from sincere commitment.
plain: A style: saying one thing while meaning another, or holding beliefs at arm's length instead of stating them sincerely.

label: Abstract vs material
description: Stance on what reality is made of: mind and ideas, or matter.
plain: Is reality, at bottom, made of ideas, mind or spirit, or of matter and physical conditions? +5 means fully idealist (ideas or spirit come first), 0 is neutral or mixed, −5 means fully materialist (matter comes first). This is a position the idea takes, not a family it belongs to.

label: Hierarchy
description: Stance toward ranked order: social, political or cosmic.
plain: Does this idea think some people, beings or powers rightly stand above others? +5 strongly favors hierarchy, 0 is neutral or mixed, −5 strongly opposes it. This is a position the idea takes, not a family it belongs to.
